Title: Role-preset edits propagate to already-logged-in users on next load
Preconditions: A currently logged-in Teacher; Admin access to edit the "teacher" role preset.
Test Steps:
1. As Admin, grant an additional module to the "teacher" role preset.
2. As the already-logged-in Teacher (same open session), reload the app.

Actual Result: CONFIRMED AS INTENTIONAL DESIGN, not a defect -- reclassified from Fail to Investigate since the code is working as written, but the test case title asserts the opposite behavior, so this needs a product-spec decision, not a code fix. UsersController.ApplyPermissionPreset (235-254) -> UserService.SetPermissionsAsync (414+) COPIES a preset permissions into per-user SubAdminPermission rows at the moment it is applied -- a one-time snapshot (comment at 444-445 confirms this is deliberate). AuthService.LoadPermissionClaimsAsync: for SubAdmin-type users (every preset role -- management, coordinator, etc.), login ALWAYS reads the frozen snapshot, never re-resolving from RoleDefinition. Only the 4 fixed system roles (Admin/Teacher/Parent/AdmissionTeam) re-resolve live each login. DECISION NEEDED: if live-sync is actually wanted, fix is in LoadPermissionClaimsAsync (check RoleDefinitionId first, fall back to frozen snapshot for hand-edited users). If copy-on-apply is intentional, this test case expected-behavior should be corrected instead.

Title: Removing a permission mid-session blocks the very next matching call
Preconditions: A Sub Admin currently able to perform some action (e.g. edit courses).
Test Steps:
1. As Admin, revoke `CourseBatchManagement:Edit` from this Sub Admin's preset.
2. As the Sub Admin (reload to pick up new claims per TC-PERM-006), attempt to edit a course.
Expected Result: 403 after reload — confirms revocation is enforced, not just granting.
Actual Result: DUPLICATE of BUG-SEC-001 -- same root cause, same fix, tracked as one dev ticket. CONFIRMED SECURITY GAP, root cause identified. Granted ReportsAnalytics:canView to a fresh SubAdmin, logged in, confirmed 200 on a gated endpoint. Revoked canView=False (204, DB state confirmed flipped via admin GET). SAME still-active token continued getting 200 on the same endpoint 3+ seconds later -- not a propagation delay, a persistent stale-access window. Contrast: TC-AUTH-007 confirmed full account deactivation DOES block the token immediately (401). ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via code, not JWT claims as first hypothesized -- decoded token has only sub/email/role, no permission claims): api/Auth/PermissionAuthorization.cs PermissionAuthorizationHandler.HandleRequirementAsync (18-35) checks only context.User.HasClaim(...) against claims embedded in the JWT at issuance (api/Auth/JwtTokenService.cs CreateToken, line 36) -- no DB lookup, no cache, nothing invalidated on revoke. application/Services/AuthService.cs LoadPermissionClaimsAsync (192-215) reads permissions once, at login only. Contrast: api/Program.cs OnTokenValidated (143-158) re-queries User.Status from the DB on EVERY request -- this is why deactivation is live and fine-grained permissions aren't. FIX: either add a live per-request permission check mirroring OnTokenValidated's Status check, or add a revocation/version stamp on the user checked at validation and bumped on every PUT /api/users/{id}/permissions call. | RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-26: FIXED (commit 88564b1, 2026-08-16). Program.cs OnTokenValidated now re-fetches role+permissions live from the DB on every request (not just at login) via AuthService.GetCurrentAccessAsync, and replaces the stale claims on the request principal before PermissionAuthorizationHandler evaluates them. Traced the full chain: handler reads context.User.HasClaim(...) against the same principal OnTokenValidated just refreshed.

Data/DatabaseInitializer.cs SystemRoleSeeds() (364-372) intends the 'management' preset to include this grant (comment confirms it exists specifically for /management/revenue). FIX: move the healing invariant out of startup-only -- either enforce it inside RoleService.UpdateAsync (refuse or auto-append CourseBatchManagement:View when saving the management preset), or run the backfill on a schedule/on-demand instead of boot-only. | RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-26: FIXED (commit f00cd78, 2026-08-16). GET /api/parent-portal/resources/{id}/download (Parent) and GET /api/resources/{id}/mine/download (Teacher) are the CORRECT, working, grant/ownership-checked endpoints -- both verified 200 with real file bytes this session. Backend logic (ParentPortalService.GetResourceForDownloadAsync, application/Services/ParentPortalService.cs lines 240-286) is correct. The actual defect: src/features/parent/Resources.tsx imports and calls downloadResource() from api/resources.ts, which hits the ADMIN-ONLY GET /api/resources/{id}/download (403 for non-Admin/SubAdmin by design, ResourcesController.cs lines 121-136) instead of the already-existing downloadParentResource() in api/parentPortal.ts (lines 49-57), which even has a code comment explicitly warning against this exact mistake: 'Not the admin-only /api/resources/{id}/download (that route 403s for any non-Admin/SubAdmin role)'. FIX: swap the import/call in Resources.tsx (parent) from downloadResource to downloadParentResource -- a one-line change. Teacher side was a false positive in this session's own testing (called the admin-only route directly instead of through the app); the real Teacher UI already calls the correct downloadMyResource(). | RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-26: FIXED (commit c277108, 2026-08-16), confirmed still on main. Parent Resources.tsx now calls downloadParentResource() from api/parentPortal.ts as originally recommended.

Title: Floating Notes button overlaps real page content (mobile, tablet, and desktop)
Actual Result: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-16: STILL PRESENT. src/components/FloatingNotes.tsx renders the notes trigger as position:fixed (bottom-20 right-4 on mobile, sm:bottom-6 sm:right-6 on desktop/tablet, confirmed via source lines 214-223) without the page reserving matching bottom padding/safe-area for its own scrollable content. Result: whenever real content happens to scroll to that fixed screen position, the button sits on top of it rather than floating above clear space. Confirmed overlapping real content on three separate occasions this session: mobile (390px) Admin > Users list -- covers part of the Joined date on a user card; tablet (820px) Teacher dashboard -- covers part of the Payout Snapshot Deductions/Waiting Added figures; desktop (1440px) SubAdmin dashboard -- covers the top-right corner of the Full module access card. FIX: give the page content a bottom padding/margin equal to the FAB height + its offset (e.g. padding-bottom: calc(3rem + 1.5rem) on the scrollable content container) so the last rows of content never render underneath the fixed button, on all three breakpoints. | RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-26: FIXED (commit b688a33, 2026-08-16), postdates this row's same-day recheck. Replaced static padding with runtime collision detection (elementsFromPoint) that fades the button toward transparent whenever it overlaps real content.

Title: Upload dialog hint text is inconsistent and inaccurate across 3 screens, none matching the real backend limits
Actual Result: Three separate hardcoded upload-hint strings exist in the frontend, each stating a DIFFERENT file-type/size limit, and none matches the real backend behavior: (1) src/components/FileDropzone.tsx line 13 default fallback = "PDF, PNG, JPG up to 10MB"; (2) src/features/teacher/Resources.tsx line 251 = "PDF, PNG, JPG, MP4 up to 25MB"; (3) src/features/admin/Resources.tsx line 233 = "PDF, DOCX, MP4 up to 50MB". Confirmed via a real 400 response earlier this session that the backend actually accepts a much broader set: .doc, .docx, .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .mov, .mp3, .mp4, .pdf, .png, .ppt, .pptx, .txt, .wav, .webm, .webp, .xls, .xlsx, .zip -- none of the three hints mention audio, spreadsheets, presentations, zip, gif/webp, or txt, all of which are actually accepted. None of the three size figures (10/25/50MB) matches the 100MB cap referenced elsewhere in this test suite (TC-ADM-052, TC-SEC-005 titles), suggesting the real/intended cap may be 100MB and all three UI hints understate it. No accept attribute is set on the underlying file input, so users are not actually blocked from uploading unlisted types -- this is a copy-accuracy bug, not a functional block, but it likely causes users to avoid trying valid file types/sizes because the UI undersells what is supported. | RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-26: FIXED (commit b688a33, 2026-08-16), postdates this row's same-day recheck. FileDropzone now has one accurate, shared default hint reflecting the real 100MB cap and full allowlist; the two screen-specific overrides were removed.

Title: Multiple real session-completion accruals sum correctly in one payout
Actual Result: Completed 3 real sessions (each SessionEarning=800 at the active rate) on top of an existing payout that already had a StudentNoShowWaiting item (800). Payout total after all 4 accruals: 3200.00, exactly 800+800+800+800. Confirmed via GET /api/payouts showing all 4 line items and the correct running total -- no drift, no double-counting, no item lost.

Title: Payout amount is preserved exactly through the full Pending -> Finalized -> Paid lifecycle
Actual Result: Took the 3200.00 payout from TC-CALC-001 through both status transitions: finalize (200, status=Finalized, total=3200.00) then mark-paid (200, status=Paid, total=3200.00). Amount identical at every stage, no rounding drift across two real state transitions.

Title: Mark Paid is correctly blocked on a non-finalized (Pending) payout
Actual Result: POST /api/payouts/{id}/mark-paid on a Pending (not yet finalized) payout with total=800.00 correctly rejected: 400 "Only a finalized payout can be marked as paid." Enforces the Pending -> Finalized -> Paid order; cannot skip a step.

Title: A session cannot be marked no-show twice, or after being marked Completed (prevents double-accrual)
Actual Result: Marking the same session no-show a second time correctly rejected: 400 A session in status 'TeacherNoShow' cannot be marked as a no-show. Separately, attempting to mark an already-Completed session (SessionEarning already accrued) as a no-show is also correctly rejected: 400 A session in status 'Completed' cannot be marked as a no-show. Both paths prevent a single session from ever accruing two payout items.

Title: Partial refunds track the running total exactly and block over-refunding at the exact boundary
Actual Result: On a real 1000.00 fully-paid invoice: refunded 300.00 (approved, alreadyRefunded correctly became 300.00). Attempted a further 800.00 refund (300+800=1100 > 1000 paid) -- correctly rejected: 400 "Refund of 800 would exceed the transaction amount of 1000.00 (300.00 already requested/refunded)," with the exact real numbers embedded in the message. Then refunded exactly the true remainder, 700.00 -- approved cleanly, alreadyRefunded became exactly 1000.00 (300+700), matching the original payment to the cent with no drift at the boundary.

Title: Package plan price changes apply prospectively only, never rewriting historical invoices
Actual Result: Raised English - Monthly plan price from 1500 to 1800. Cancelled and renewed a real existing subscription on that plan -- the fresh invoice generated by the renewal correctly billed at the NEW price (1800.00). All of that same parent's prior invoices (1000.00, 999.00 from earlier tests, issued before the price change) remained completely unchanged at their original amounts -- confirmed no retroactive rewrite of already-issued invoices when the master plan price is edited.
